posts.text:
I think one of the most important things people can work on in life is learning how to control their emotions. It can make a tremendous difference in how you think, how you communicate, how you handle difficult situations, and how people perceive you.

Emotional intelligence is something I think gets overlooked way too often. You can be extremely knowledgeable and intelligent, but if you can’t control your emotions, it can completely undermine that intelligence.

Take debating or having a disagreement with someone, for example. If you want to be taken seriously, you have to learn how to keep your composure. The moment you resort to insults, name-calling, or personal attacks, you’ve already weakened your argument. It doesn’t make you look smarter or more convincing. Quite honestly, it does the opposite. You can have a legitimate point, but the way you deliver it can completely discredit what you’re trying to say.

And I’m not saying any of this as if I’ve always been good at it. I’ve been guilty of it myself. But over time, after being mentored, observing some very intelligent and well-respected men and how they carry themselves, and doing some reading through self-help and personal development books, it really started changing the way I think and respond to people.

I honestly feel like it made a dramatic difference in me.

There’s nothing wrong with disagreeing with someone. There’s nothing wrong with standing your ground or defending what you believe. But you can do all of that without losing your composure or disrespecting someone.

In fact, I think there’s a lot more strength in being able to remain calm when someone is trying to get under your skin than there is in firing back with insults.
